BiblicalUsage: This word is a view or appearance, and Nebuchadnezzar uses it for the great tree of his dream, whose height reaches to heaven and whose sight is to the end of all the earth. Daniel repeats the same words when he interprets it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the tree's great sight is the pride of the king, and the sight that reaches to the ends of the earth is the pride God cuts down.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
